title: Replacing a finite block in an arbitrary module basis
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $F$ be a free $R$-module with basis $\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with no restriction on the cardinality of $\mathcal B$. Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and distinct $e_1,\ldots,e_n\in\mathcal B$, and put $T=\operatorname{span}_R(\mathcal B\setminus\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\})$. Suppose $y_1,\ldots,y_n\in F$ satisfy $y_i=\sum_{j=1}^n b_{ij}e_j+t_i$ with $t_i\in T$, and the matrix $B=(b_{ij})$ [def-weil-matrix] is invertible, meaning that an $n\times n$ matrix $V$ satisfies $BV=VB=I_n$. Then the $R$-linear endomorphism $U$ of $F$ sending $e_i$ to $y_i$ and fixing the other original basis vectors is an automorphism. The family indexed by the original basis indices, with each $e_i$ replaced by $y_i$ and all other vectors fixed, is a basis of $F$. If $G=\operatorname{span}_R\{y_1,\ldots,y_n\}$, then $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ is a basis of $G$ and $F=G\oplus T$, where the latter equality means that every element of $F$ has a unique expression $g+t$ with $g\in G$ and $t\in T$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof second paragraph (invertible finite-coordinate matrix gives a basis replacement and a free summand of the ambient module)

proof.text: Write $C=\mathcal B\setminus\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}$. By the unique finite-coordinate description of a basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], every $x\in F$ has a unique expression $x=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i e_i+\sum_{c\in C}d_c c$ with $(d_c)$ finitely supported. Assign arbitrary images to the original basis vectors and define the resulting map on $x$ by the same finite linear combination of their assigned images. Uniqueness of coordinates and coordinatewise addition and scalar multiplication show directly that this gives a unique linear map. Use this construction for $U(e_i)=y_i$, $U(c)=c$, and for $W(e_i)=\sum_{j=1}^n v_{ij}(e_j-t_j)$, $W(c)=c$, where $V=(v_{ij})$ is the given inverse of $B$. Both maps fix $T$ pointwise, since each element of $T$ is a finite linear combination of elements of $C$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof second paragraph: the asserted isomorphism sending the selected basis vectors to their projective components; explicit inverse calculation supplied by Q56

proof.text:
For each selected basis vector, finite distributivity gives
$$UW(e_i)=\sum_j v_{ij}\bigl(U(e_j)-U(t_j)\bigr)=\sum_j v_{ij}(y_j-t_j)=\sum_{j,k}v_{ij}b_{jk}e_k=\sum_k(VB)_{ik}e_k=e_i.$$
For $c\in C$ both maps fix $c$, so $UW(c)=c$. Applying linearity to the finite basis expansion of any $x$ proves $UW(x)=x$. Here the order $VB$ is deliberate: the statement writes the coordinates of $y_i$ in row $i$, rather than column $i$.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof second paragraph: the asserted isomorphism sending the selected basis vectors to their projective components; explicit inverse calculation supplied by Q56

proof.text:
The other composite on the selected vectors is
$$WU(e_i)=W(y_i)=\sum_j b_{ij}W(e_j)+t_i=\sum_{j,k}b_{ij}v_{jk}(e_k-t_k)+t_i=\sum_k(BV)_{ik}(e_k-t_k)+t_i=e_i.$$
On every $c\in C$ it is again the identity. Thus $WU=1_F$ by the same finite expansion. Consequently the linear maps $U,W$ are mutual inverses, proving that $U$ is an automorphism. These formulas also cover $n=0$: the sums are empty and both maps fix the entire original basis.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof second paragraph: the asserted isomorphism sending the selected basis vectors to their projective components; explicit inverse calculation supplied by Q56

proof.text: The image family is a basis by the definition [def-weil-pbc-free-module], as follows without any basis-transport theorem. Given $x\in F$, expand $W(x)$ in the original basis and apply $U$; this gives a finite expression for $x$ in the family $(y_1,\ldots,y_n,(c)_{c\in C})$ indexed by the original indices. If two finite coefficient families give the same $x$, apply $W$ to their expressions. Since $W(y_i)=e_i$ and $W(c)=c$, uniqueness of the original basis coordinates makes those coefficient families equal. This proves precisely existence and uniqueness of finite coordinates for the image family.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, proof second paragraph: the asserted isomorphism sending the selected basis vectors to their projective components; explicit inverse calculation supplied by Q56

proof.text: By definition of $G$, every $g\in G$ is a finite linear combination of the $y_i$. Any two such expressions extend by zero on $C$ to expressions in the basis from step 4, so their coefficients agree; hence $(y_i)_{i=1}^n$ is a basis of $G$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For arbitrary $x$, split its new basis expression into its selected terms $g$ and its remaining terms $t$; then $x=g+t$ with $g\in G$, $t\in T$. If also $x=g'+t'$, express $g,g'$ in the $y_i$ and $t,t'$ in $C$. Uniqueness in the same indexed basis gives equality of the selected coefficients and of the complementary coefficients, so $g=g'$ and $t=t'$. This is the stated meaning of $F=G\oplus T$, including $G=0$, $T=F$ when $n=0$.

lean.statement: theorem finite_block_replacement {R : Type u} {F : Type v} {ι : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup F] [Module R F] (b : Module.Basis ι R F) (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ↪ ι) (y t : Fin n → F) (B V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) (ht : ∀ i, t i ∈ Submodule.span R (b '' (Set.range e)ᶜ)) (hy : ∀ i, y i = (∑ j : Fin n, B i j • b (e j)) + t i) (hBV : B * V = 1) (hVB : V * B = 1) : (∃ U : F ≃ₗ[R] F, (∀ i, U (b (e i)) = y i) ∧ ∀ j, j ∉ Set.range e → U (b j) = b j) ∧ (∃ b' : Module.Basis ι R F, (∀ i, b' (e i) = y i) ∧ ∀ j, j ∉ Set.range e → b' j = b j) ∧ (∃ c : Module.Basis (Fin n) R (Submodule.span R (Set.range y)), ∀ i, (c i : F) = y i) ∧ ∀ x : F, ∃! p : (Submodule.span R (Set.range y)) × (Submodule.span R (b '' (Set.range e)ᶜ)), x = (p.1 : F) + (p.2 : F)
